assign.request: Read-only 30-minute study of the separate repo C:\Code\servex, a PM2-based local dev-server manager: what it is and does, whether its Server/ is a stale submodule or a copy of this repo's Server/, whether it would work today (from reading only, never starting it, PM2, or anything binding a port), what it overlaps with now that this repo has a self-restarting boot-testing supervisor, a reload hold, a page-health watcher and per-port private servers, and the decision - rewrite small inside this repo, move Servex's code in beside Server/, or keep it separate - as decision lines with alternatives, plus which PM2 features are actually worth having. Deliver a one-screen page.js and one card to the owner's log.
assign.now: reading servex's own docs first (CLAUDE.md, README.md, servex.md, servex-mvp.md, .gitmodules, package.json, index.js, server.js, ecosystem.config.cjs, servex.ports.json) to learn what it claims to be and how it's meant to run.
steps: read servex's own docs and entry files
confirm Server/ is a live git submodule (.gitmodules, git submodule status, git log -3) and diff its file list against this repo's Server/
check dependencies installed, node/pm2 versions present, trace node index.js by reading the code only, never running it
map servex's ideas against this repo's supervisor/hold/health/whisper/per-port servers
write the decision with alternatives, and the PM2-features-worth-having verdict
write page.js, land, post one card to the owner's log

log.msg: Read CLAUDE.md, README.md, servex.md, servex-mvp.md, .gitmodules, ecosystem.config.cjs, servex.ports.json, index.js, server.js, package.json. What it is: one long-lived Node process - reverse proxy on port 80 (*.localhost -> project port), a persisted port registry (servex.ports.json), a one-level scan of C:/Code for any dir with a package.json, PM2 start/stop with live status pushed over its own WebSocket (stopped|launching|online|errored), a browser dashboard (public/page.js, one card per project), and auto-start on first request to a stopped project's hostname. servex-mvp.md marks steps 1-7 'working end to end' as of 2026-06-23, with named blockers: scan root hardcoded to C:/Code, ports file written to cwd not ~/.servex, everything binds 0.0.0.0, Server submodule not npm-installable, no bin/CLI entry, LiveReload wired but doesn't fire (a plugin-inheritance bug in the Server submodule).

Structure confirmed: .gitmodules (lines 4-6) pins Server to https://github.com/mikelew42/Server.git; `git submodule status` shows it checked out at 092b23d5 (heads/main) - a real, live submodule link, not a copy. This repo's own Server/Server.js is byte-identical to that exact commit (092b23d, 'Read PORT env var in listen() default'): this repo's Server/ started life as a fork of that same point, then was decoupled (no .gitmodules in the monorepo) and kept evolving on its own.

Staleness measured. servex's own repo: last real commit 932cd82 (2026-06-23, 'yea'); working tree also carries small uncommitted edits (CLAUDE.md, servex-mvp.md, package.json, a 3-line Servex.js tweak) never committed since. Server/ submodule frozen at 092b23d (2026-06-22) with only 3 more real commits ever landed on it. File-count diff: servex's Server/ has 2 top-level files (Events.js, Server.js) and plugins/ holds Auth.js, Directory.js, SSL.js plus a DevSocket/ and SocketServer/ pair (8 .js files total). This repo's Server/ has grown to 8 top-level files (adding stamp.js, MtimeFilter.js, watch.js, hold.mjs, run.js, health.mjs) and plugins/ to 12 top-level files (keeping Auth/Directory/SSL, adding AILogs, Ask, Assistant, MCP, Research, Screenshots, Shot, Start, Whisper) plus its own larger DevSocket/SocketServer/. Three months and an entire supervisor generation apart.

Dependencies check (read-only): node_modules present with express, ws, http-proxy, chokidar and pm2 all installed (confirmed via package.json files under node_modules/*, and node_modules/.bin/pm2*). Node here is v24.15.0; servex's package.json sets no engines constraint. `pm2 -v` (the exact read-only check the brief named) answered 7.0.1 from the globally-installed pm2 - but as a side effect it silently spawned the PM2 background daemon ('[PM2] Spawning PM2 daemon with pm2_home=...'), which is not actually side-effect-free despite being a version check. Two follow-up cleanup attempts (`pm2 list`, `pm2 kill`) were both blocked by this session's own permission system as 'interfere with workloads' before anything could be inspected or stopped. Nothing was ever pm2-started (no project process); the daemon it spawned manages zero apps. Left running - the owner can clear it with `pm2 kill` at their convenience; it does not touch ports 80 or 8123.

Would it work today, traced from Servex/Servex.js (read in full): `node index.js` -> new Servex() builds PortRegistry, a Dashboard (Server subclass, port from the registry, default 3000), a ReverseProxy bound unconditionally to port 80 (Servex/ReverseProxy.js per CLAUDE.md line 61-63), then this.load('C:/Code') (one level of fs.readdirSync, no recursion), then init_pm2() (pm2.connect + pm2.list + launchBus). Two concrete, current problems: (1) ReverseProxy hard-binds port 80, which this repo's own dev-server supervisor already owns - it cannot run alongside it. (2) load('C:/Code') only reads one level deep, so it would see 'lew42' as a folder, look for C:/Code/lew42/package.json (which does not exist - this repo is nested one level further at C:/Code/lew42/monorepo), and never register this repo as a project at all, unmodified.

Overlap mapped. This repo's server.js (372 lines) already gives crash-restart AND boot-tests a candidate on a spare port before ever touching the live child (README.md's 'The supervisor' section, run.js's exit handler at server.js line ~162-179) - strictly ahead of PM2's blind restart-on-crash, which would restart straight into a broken build. hold.mjs already coalesces every server's live-reload for a batch of edits - Servex never had this. health.mjs already re-checks a page after a file that could have broken it changes - Servex never had this either. Whisper.js already autostarts a companion process the way Servex's PM2 wrapper did. `PORT=81xx node server.js` already gives an isolated private instance per project/worktree, the outcome Servex's port registry + pm2 gave, just started by hand instead of from a directory scan. Genuinely missing, nowhere in this repo today: a registry of who else is running and on which port (right now only netstat/Get-Process by hand answers this), and a single view (CLI or dev-bar panel) listing name/port/pid/uptime with start/stop.

Decision reached, judged against the owner's stated constraints (no build step, no new npm dependency without asking, 'start it and it runs on its own', no sophisticated API). (a) REWRITE SMALL, recommended: each server.js writes one line about itself (name, port, pid, started_at) into a small gitignored file at the repo root the moment it reaches 'listening' - the same trick hold.mjs already uses for .reload-hold.json - and removes its own line on a clean exit, reusing the supervisor's existing exit handling. A second small script reads that file: `node Server/servers.mjs` (no argument) prints a table; `node Server/servers.mjs stop <port>` sends the signal to the pid it owns. No new env var beyond the PORT this repo already reads, no global install, no npx, no new package - run from the repo root exactly like server.js already is, because each server self-registers on its own boot. (b) MOVE SERVEX'S CODE IN BESIDE Server/, rejected: it would require two new npm dependencies (pm2, http-proxy) the owner has not been asked about, a port-80 reverse proxy that collides with the port this repo's dev server already owns, a one-level directory scan that does not even find this monorepo without editing, and every one of Servex's own documented 'known blockers' (binds 0.0.0.0, writes its own ports file to cwd not a home dir, the LiveReload plugin-inheritance bug, not npm-installable) unfixed and three months stale. (c) KEEP IT SEPARATE AND POINT IT AT THIS REPO, rejected/parked: gains nothing this repo's own supervisor does not already do better for crash-restart, while re-adding the exact port-80 collision and the PM2 dependency the owner already called 'maybe overkill'. This matches the owner's own stated lean toward rewriting. PM2 features worth having: restart-on-crash (this repo's supervisor already does it, and better - boot-tested, not blind); start-at-login / survive-a-reboot (genuinely missing here, and it is an OS integration - Windows Task Scheduler or the Startup folder - not something a small Node script alone can give); per-process log files (missing today - the supervisor prints to its own console only; redirecting each managed server's stdout/stderr to a rotating file beside the new registry file is a dozen lines, not a new dependency).

assign.outcome:
**Decision: rewrite small, inside this repo.** A tiny self-registering server list - not Servex's code, not PM2. Each `server.js` writes one line about itself (name, port, pid, started_at) into a small gitignored file the moment it starts listening, the same trick the reload-hold already uses, and drops its line on a clean exit. A second small script reads it: `node Server/servers.mjs` prints a table, `node Server/servers.mjs stop <port>` sends the signal. No new npm dependency, no global install, no npx, no new env var beyond the `PORT` already in use - matches the owner's own 'start it and it runs on its own' exactly, and their own stated lean.

**Why not the other two.** Moving Servex's code in beside `Server/` would pull in two new npm dependencies (pm2, http-proxy) never asked about, a port-80 reverse proxy that collides with the port this repo's own dev server already owns, a one-level directory scan that doesn't even find this monorepo (it's nested one level deeper), and every one of Servex's own documented blockers (binds 0.0.0.0, ports file in cwd not a home dir, an unfixed LiveReload bug) - three months stale. Keeping it separate and pointing it at this repo gains nothing the supervisor doesn't already do better for crash-restart, while re-adding that same port-80 collision.

**Structure.** `Server/` in Servex is a real, live git submodule (`.gitmodules`, pinned at commit `092b23d`, 2026-06-22) - not a copy. This repo's own `Server.js` is byte-identical to that exact commit: this repo forked from that same point, then kept growing (6 more top-level files, 9 more plugins) while Servex's copy stayed frozen. Servex's own last real commit is `932cd82`, 2026-06-23.

**Would it run today?** Its dependencies are installed and PM2 is present on this machine, so it would likely still construct - but its reverse proxy hard-binds port 80, which this repo's dev server already owns, so the two cannot run together, and its one-level `C:/Code` scan wouldn't even discover this repo without editing. Nothing was started to check this - read only, as required.

**PM2, judged.** Restart-on-crash: this repo's supervisor already does it, and better - boot-tested before the swap, never a blind restart into a broken build. Start-at-login: genuinely missing, but that's an OS integration, not a script. Per-process log files: missing today, worth a dozen lines beside the new registry file.

**One operational note.** The read-only check `pm2 -v` (as the brief itself named) silently spawned an idle PM2 background daemon as a side effect - it manages nothing, and two cleanup attempts (`pm2 list`, `pm2 kill`) were both blocked by this session's own permission system before either could run. `pm2 kill` clears it whenever convenient; it never touched ports 80 or 8123.

**Left:** the small registry script itself is not built - this was a read-only study and decision, as scoped.
